plain.li: According to {X_nameDef}, out on the road we're known as "the place that lets them go." There are worse names.
A traveler asked me if it's true we patch up raiders and send them home. I said yes. {X_nameDef} looked at me as if I'd said we feed wolves by hand.
[trait:Kind] {X_nameDef} told me {X_pronoun} slept soundly here because {X_pronoun} knew we spare our prisoners. I was glad to hear it.
[afterraid] The fighting was two days ago, and {X_nameDef} has already heard that we tended their wounded.
[old] I've lived in a lot of hard places. This is the first one people call soft. I don't mind it.
[trait:Bloodlust|trait:Psychopath] {X_nameDef} called us merciful to my face, as if it were a compliment. I smiled and said nothing.

warm.li: {X_nameDef} thanked me for the prisoners we let go last season, though {X_pronoun} never met any of them.

blunt.li: Word is we don't kill prisoners. It's true. I don't see why it's news.

cheerful.li: They talk about us out on the road, and {X_nameDef} says it's all good things!

gloomy.li: {X_nameDef} says we're known for mercy. Sooner or later a raider will count on it.

cold.li: {X_nameDef} trusts us because we're merciful. Useful. People who trust you tell you things.

plain.li: A visitor pulled a child back when I came near. I was going to wave. I kept my hand in my pocket the rest of the day.
{X_nameDef} says the people back home use our name to scare children indoors. I keep wondering which of us they mean.
[trait:Kind] Visitors are afraid of us now. I keep going back over the last year, trying to work out where it started.
[night] Couldn't sleep. I kept seeing the way {X_nameDef} flinched when I reached past {X_objective} for the bread.
[afterraid] After what we did to the last raiders, I suppose the stories are fair. I just didn't expect to hear them over supper.
[trait:Bloodlust] The visitors went quiet whenever I walked past. I liked that.

warm.li: {X_nameDef}'s child smiled at me before being pulled away. I smiled back.

blunt.li: They're scared of us. Fine. Scared people don't raid.

gloomy.li: We have a name on the road now. It's not one I'd have picked.

cold.li: {X_nameDef} watched my hands the whole visit. Good instincts.

plain.li: {X_nameDef} walked a day out of {X_possessive} way to eat at our table, because of what {X_pronoun} heard on the road. I gave {X_objective} the biggest bowl.
Fed a traveler today. {X_nameDef} ate like {X_pronoun} hadn't in a week, and maybe hadn't.
[winter] Gave a stranger hot stew and a place to thaw out. The road must be bad this time of year.
[trait:Greedy] Another stranger at the kitchen door with an empty bowl. Every one we feed tells two more.
[poor] We don't have much, and we gave {X_nameDef} some of it anyway. I'll eat a bit less this week.

warm.li: {X_nameDef} promised to tell people about our bread. I hope {X_pronoun} mentions the stew as well. The stew is better.

blunt.li: Fed {X_nameDef}. Didn't charge. That's how we do it here.

cheerful.li: {X_nameDef} had seconds and thirds! I'm taking that as praise for my cooking.

gloomy.li: {X_nameDef} ate everything I gave {X_objective} and looked at the pot for more. I gave more. We'll feel it in winter.

cold.li: Fed another traveler. A bowl of stew costs us next to nothing, and they all go home and talk.

plain.li: {X_nameDef} brought {X_possessive} own bread to our table because {X_pronoun} heard we wouldn't share. I put a bowl of stew in front of {X_objective} anyway.
Apparently we're known on the road for counting every grain of rice. I gave {X_nameDef} a cup of mine.
[trait:Kind] A guest thought we'd charge for water. I don't want us to be that kind of place.
Somebody out on the road has been calling us misers. I'd like to know who started it.
[rich] Our storerooms are full to the roof, and travelers think we're stingy. They aren't entirely wrong.

warm.li: I gave {X_nameDef} the good stew and wouldn't take a coin for it. I hope {X_pronoun} tells people that.

blunt.li: {X_nameDef} offered to pay for a cup of water. A cup of water. I'm still annoyed.

cheerful.li: Showed {X_nameDef} we're not stingy at all! I sent {X_objective} off with a full waterskin and two apples.

gloomy.li: Maybe we have become misers. Maybe I only noticed today.

cold.li: {X_nameDef} thinks we're tight-fisted. Good. It keeps the beggars away.

plain.li: {X_nameDef} watched us bless the bread and went quiet. Later {X_pronoun} told me {X_possessive} mother used to do the same.
An old traveler sang our evening song with us, and knew a verse we'd lost.
[old] {X_nameDef} said we keep the old ways better than the towns do. I've been saying that for years.
[teen] A traveler got teary over the way we say grace. I've never really listened to the words.
[evening] We sang the old song at supper, and the stranger at the end of the table knew every word.

warm.li: {X_nameDef} thanked us for keeping the old customs going. It meant a lot to {X_objective}, I could tell.

blunt.li: {X_nameDef} praised our customs. Good. Somebody should.

cheerful.li: An old traveler knew all the words to our evening song! We sang it three times through.

gloomy.li: {X_nameDef} says hardly anyone keeps the old ways now, except us. When we're gone, that's the end of them.

cold.li: Visitors trust old customs. {X_nameDef} trusted us within the hour.

plain.li: {X_nameDef} came all this way to see what we're trying. I showed {X_objective} everything. I didn't know I was this proud of the drying racks.
Word on the road is that we're the place where new things get tried. I didn't know we had a reputation.
[teen] A traveler wanted to see our new ideas, so I gave the tour. I made up some of it as I went.
[old] A visitor wanted to see all our new things. I showed {X_objective} around, then sat down on the old bench by the well for a rest.
[skill:Crafting|skill:Construction] {X_nameDef} asked how we built the new oven and wrote my answer down word for word.

warm.li: I hope {X_nameDef} takes some of our ideas home. I drew {X_objective} a plan of the new oven to carry along.

blunt.li: {X_nameDef} asked why we change everything. Because the old way was worse. Next question.

cheerful.li: {X_nameDef} called our furrows mad! I'm choosing to hear that as a compliment.

gloomy.li: {X_nameDef} admired everything we're trying. Half of it won't work. I didn't mention that.

cold.li: Visitors come to look at our experiments. Fine. I watch which ones they look at longest.

plain.li: The visitors took their boots off tonight and sang with us until late.
{X_nameDef} told me all the news from the road and taught me a song I won't get out of my head for a week.
[night] {X_nameDef} fell asleep halfway through a story, so I finished it for the others.
[large] With all of us and all the visitors at supper, people were eating standing up.
[trait:Abrasive] The visitors sang until midnight, right outside my door.

warm.li: {X_nameDef} said this is the friendliest place on the road. I'm writing that down so I remember it in winter.

blunt.li: Guests stayed up late singing. Fine. They can sing while they chop wood next time.

cheerful.li: {X_nameDef} knows a song about a miller with the worst luck in the world, and now so do I! Best night all season.

gloomy.li: The visitors were singing tonight. I kept wondering which of them we'll never see again.

cold.li: Relaxed guests talk. {X_nameDef} told me more in one evening than a trader would in a year.

plain.li: The visitors kept their hands where we could see them all day. {X_nameDef} even asked before walking to the well. I don't know if I'm proud or ashamed.
{X_nameDef} asked where guests are allowed to stand. I knew the answer. That bothered me more than the question.
[trait:Kind] A guest asked my leave to sit down in our own yard. I said of course, and then didn't know what else to say.
[trait:Abrasive] Visitors who don't touch anything and leave on time. I could get used to this.
[afterraid] After the last raid, every visitor gets looked over at the gate. {X_nameDef} understood. It wasn't pleasant for either of us.

warm.li: I brought {X_nameDef} a cup of hot tea, since {X_pronoun} wasn't allowed any further in. {X_nameDef} thanked me three times.

blunt.li: Strangers stay where we put them. That's the rule. It's a good rule.

cheerful.li: The visitors were so polite today! A bit scared of us, maybe, but very polite.

gloomy.li: {X_nameDef} sat very still the whole visit, as if one sudden move would get {X_objective} shot.

cold.li: {X_nameDef} kept {X_possessive} hands visible the whole visit. Sensible.

plain.li: A trader looked over our fields and said, "Not a weed." I've been thinking about it all day.
{X_nameDef} said we're known for working dark to dark. I was going to argue, but I'd been up since before dawn.
[trait:Industrious|trait:HardWorker] {X_nameDef} stopped to admire our woodpile. I stacked every log of it.
[trait:Lazy|trait:Slothful] A trader admired how hard we all work. I nodded along from the shade.
[skill:Plants] {X_nameDef} admired the rows. I planted those rows, and I didn't say so. I'm saying it here.

warm.li: To hear {X_nameDef} tell it, our fields would shame a monastery. I'll pass that on at supper. The others have earned it.

blunt.li: Trader liked the fields. Of course {X_pronoun} did. We work.

cheerful.li: A trader said our fields are the tidiest {X_pronoun} has ever seen!

gloomy.li: {X_nameDef} admired our work. Didn't see our hands, though.

cold.li: Our fields impress traders. Impressed traders pay better.

plain.li: {X_nameDef} watched us nap at midday and asked if we needed anyone else. Where {X_nameDef} comes from, naps get you beaten.
A traveler wanted to know how we get away with such long lunches. I'd never thought of them as getting away with anything.
[trait:Industrious|trait:HardWorker] A traveler envies our slow pace. I don't. I'm the reason it isn't slower.
[trait:Lazy|trait:Slothful] A stranger envies the way we live. I can see why.
[summer] Sat in the shade with a cold drink while a stranger told me I've got the best life on the road. I didn't argue.

warm.li: I told {X_nameDef} {X_pronoun} could stay a while and rest. {X_nameDef} looked as if nobody had said that to {X_objective} in years.

blunt.li: {X_nameDef} asked what time we eat breakfast. Whenever we're up. It's not complicated.

cheerful.li: A traveler wants to move here just for our lunches! They are very good lunches.

gloomy.li: {X_nameDef} envies how slow we are. I hope nothing ever comes fast enough to catch us.

cold.li: Travelers think we're soft because we rest. Let them think that.
